Subject: Debrief: Daniel Park — Eng Manager (final round) - score collection & closure

Hi all,

Thanks for taking the time this week to interview Daniel (final round). I pulled together the consolidated scorecard and my brief calibration notes — attaching both. Please do two quick things by EOD Tue (tomorrow):

- Add your final hire/reject vote in the scorecard PDF (page 1) or reply with a one-liner (hire/lean hire/lean no/no) + 1 sentence rationale.
- If you flagged any must-have concerns (security, ops/on-call depth, leadership gaps), call them out explicitly so we can decide corrective items in the offer or decline.

Context: hiring manager (Jonas) is leaning but requested more clarity on system-design depth for high-concurrency failover. We need a majority + 1 for a clear hire; if we land on a tie, can someone volunteer to own the tiebreak + 15 min sync?

Attachments: [Attachment: Scorecard_Daniel_Park.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: calibration_notes_engr_mgr.txt (txt)].

Quick bullets from my read:
- Strengths: cross-team empathy, mentoring examples, shipping roadmap clarity.
- Risks: limited examples of live-ops debugging at scale and some gap on emergency runbook ownership.

If we can close votes tomorrow by 5pm PT I will draft the decision and next steps (offer parameters or rejection note) on Wednesday.

Best,
Marissa

Vote: HIRE (5/5)
Quick rationale: Daniel gave concrete examples of ownership — shipped cross-region failover feature at Nimbus that reduced mean recovery time. He asked the right probing questions on tradeoffs and annotated rollbacks. The on-call examples were not as deep as I'd like for a platform manager, but his leadership and ability to drive incident playbooks is strong.

Action: If we want to shore up the on-call risk, offer with 6-month IC check-in + runbook ownership expectation (documented) seems reasonable.

Marissa / team —

Vote: LEAN NO

Full rationale (quick): I appreciated Daniel's PM collaboration stories and people ops; however, when I pushed on high-concurrency design and live escalation examples, his answers were conceptual and lacked a clear play-by-play of a real incident he directly owned. For a manager who will inherit our paging and multi-region failover, I need stronger evidence of incident command AND postmortem depth.

I added detailed notes in the attachment [jonas_weber_notes_dp.docx] with the specific follow-up questions and the gaps I saw (pages 2-3). If others think calibration differences explain this, happy to join a 15-minute sync to align.

Jonas Weber
Dir., Platform Engineering

Thanks for the quick turn. Tally so far: Aditya (HIRE), Mina (HIRE), Laura (no response), Jonas (LEAN NO). That puts us at majority HIRE but with a clear ops/incident risk flagged by Jonas.

Decision path:
- We will extend an offer contingent on a documented 90-day plan that includes: ownership of one runbook walkthrough, leading a simulated war-room drill, and a 6-month check-in focused on live-ops readiness.
- Jonas: would you be comfortable with that corrective plan documented as a condition, or do you prefer we decline? If you prefer decline, say so and I'll stop the offer flow.
- Laura: please send your vote by EOD if you have one — otherwise I'll proceed with drafting the offer for manager approval by 5pm PT.

Next steps (I will action):
- Draft offer with the conditional items and proposed compensation band (23-25 total comp) and share for manager approval by 3pm PT.
- Hannah (recruiter): please standby for candidate communication — I will loop you into the offer doc.
- If a tie or explicit decline appears from Jonas, we will schedule Mina's suggested 15-min calibration (Mina offered times above).

Thanks,
Marissa
